title: NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (November 2026) — builder confidence, 10:00 a.m. ET, the day before housing starts
source: EST: nahb.org/news-and-economics/housing-economics/indices/nahb-wells-fargo-housing-market-index-release-dates fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 47,120 bytes) — the publisher's own "2026 HMI Schedule" table, standing note "Normal release time: 10:00 AM Eastern Time", row "Nov. 2026 | November 17, 2026"; the same table's already-elapsed 2026 rows (July 16, August 17, September 16, October 19) are consistent with the third-Monday-or-Tuesday convention and with the August edition NAHB published 2026-08-17. Filed `estimate` per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep, not because the source is weak — NAHB is the producer of this series, not an aggregator, and the existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 precedent (a publisher's own forward calendar carrying IR:/confirmed) is available to whichever lane researches this id. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the housing-starts-2026-11-18 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). Why it earns its own row rather than a line in that ledger: it is a SERIES THIS CALENDAR TRACKS NOWHERE — the same criterion the housing-starts-2026-12-17 lane used to propose new-home-sales-2026-12-23 — and it is the one residential release that is directly ABOUT homebuilders rather than about federal counts. That matters precisely because the residential ledgers keep concluding `symbols: []` on federal prints: this lane re-derived that ITB's overnight gap on 515 Census release dates has been null since 2015 (2016-20 p=0.50, 2021-26 p=0.21), and the untested alternative is that builder SENTIMENT, not builder DATA, is the homebuilder-keyed channel. Nobody here has measured it, and the NAHB series is the instrument for it. Distinguishing features beyond newness: it publishes 10:00 ET on the day BEFORE New Residential Construction every month, so it is the standing D-1 leading indicator for the print (NAHB publishes the HMI-vs-single-family-starts chart itself); the current reading is 35 (August 2026, up one point), deeply below the 50 neutral line and consistent with the starts series' 1,239,000 SAAR July print; and it is privately produced, so unlike every Census and BLS release in this corridor it carries NO funding-cliff exposure — which makes it the one residential read that survives a lapse. One caution recorded so it is not rediscovered: 2026-11-17 is already the corridor's heaviest morning (retail sales 08:30, industrial production, import/export prices, MTIS 10:00), so a 10:00 HMI lands buried; whether it is separable on that specific session is a question for its own initial research and this lane did not test it. NAHB's PDF schedule link (`/-/media/NAHB/.../hmi-release-schedule.pdf`) returns HTTP 200 with an HTML body — the same 404-served-as-200 trap the sibling lane recorded for the Atlanta Fed paths; the HTML release-dates page above is the working source. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
